item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-a6180d39c11c1a66","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"On 2 March 2023, President Lula issued Provisional Measure 1.164 establishing Bolsa Família to replace Auxílio Brasil. The measure defined objectives of combating hunger, interrupting intergenerational poverty, and protecting children, adolescents, and young people through coordinated federal, state, and municipal implementation, SUAS integration, social participation, and use of CadÚnico.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly enacted during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measure was issued by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva under constitutional authority.","limitations":["The supplied text establishes the program's design and legal enactment, not its full-year implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a6180d39c11c1a66","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The 2023 Bolsa Família law set eligibility at household per-capita income of up to R$218, retained families for up to 24 months after income increases under specified conditions, and created a benefit structure including R$142 per household member, a minimum household amount of R$600, R$150 per child in early childhood, and R$50 for eligible pregnant women, children, and adolescents.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly specified in the March 2023 measure, with relevant provisions taking effect in June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The benefit rules were enacted through Lula's provisional measure.","limitations":["The document does not report actual coverage, uptake, or distributional outcomes during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a6180d39c11c1a66","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The 2023 Bolsa Família framework conditioned continued benefits on prenatal care, vaccination, nutritional monitoring for young children, and minimum school attendance, while prohibiting punitive or humiliating procedures for noncompliance. It created decentralized management, an indexed performance and funding mechanism for subnational administrators, public beneficiary information, local social-control councils, and a federal inspection network.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.5","6B.7","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly enacted during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The institutional controls and conditionality rules were established in Lula's measure.","limitations":["The supplied text does not show whether monitoring, inspections, or local councils functioned effectively in practice during the year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a6180d39c11c1a66","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The Bolsa Família measure required repayment of benefits obtained through deliberately false CadÚnico information, allowed notification through multiple channels, required inflation updating of debts, referred suspected fraud by public officials for police investigation, and provided for unpaid amounts to enter federal active debt.","question_ids":["5B.5","6B.5","7B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly enacted during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These anti-fraud and recovery provisions were enacted by Lula's government.","limitations":["No enforcement cases or recovery results are supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a6180d39c11c1a66","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The measure converted CadÚnico into a public electronic registry, required or permitted interoperability with the national social-security database, imposed confidentiality commitments on accessing bodies, and was signed by Lula on 2 March 2023.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.9","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly enacted during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Lula signed the measure establishing these administrative and data-governance provisions.","limitations":["The document does not establish the quality of data protection or interoperability after enactment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e008fe023a58d1c3","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"A government-commissioned evaluation of Bolsa Família reported a positive cost-benefit ratio: each R$1 invested was estimated to return R$1.085 to society, or an 8.5% return. The study also associated the program with reduced school repetition and estimated returns through employment-income, health, education, and taxation channels.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The page was published in 2022 and describes an evaluation intended to inform subsequent policy; it is contextual evidence available during Lula's 2023 period, not a 2023 outcome.","ruler_attribution":"The evaluation was produced within the federal social-development administration, but predates Lula's 2023 administration.","limitations":["The supplied page does not provide the full study, methodology details, or a 2023-specific causal estimate."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e008fe023a58d1c3","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"The Bolsa Família evaluation stated that simulations supported expanding beneficiary numbers, eliminating the waiting list, and increasing the average benefit, while warning that combining both expansions would place the average benefit around R$220–R$250; under budget constraints it recommended increasing coverage while maintaining current average benefits.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.9","6B.5","8B.1","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The simulation was published in 2022 and is a pre-2023 policy input rather than evidence of a 2023 decision or result.","ruler_attribution":"The study was commissioned by the federal social-development administration before Lula's 2023 term.","limitations":["The supplied document does not show whether Lula adopted the modeled recommendation or how fiscal constraints affected implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-776a344c8b828b56","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"The government-linked NUCLEP describes Brazil's PROSUB as developing the country's first nuclear-propelled submarine, the Almirante Álvaro Alberto, with NUCLEP manufacturing the Block 40 prototype section containing the reactor and associated equipment; the submarine is described as intended for submarine hunting and not carrying ballistic missiles.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.5","1B.10","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The page is undated and describes a long-running program; it does not establish a specific 2023 presidential decision.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies the Brazilian state and Navy program but does not attribute the described construction decision specifically to Lula in 2023.","limitations":["No 2023 funding, safety, inspection, command-and-control, or operational-posture evidence is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9f4a8cfb7e0796b6","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"In a 23 May 2023 Security Council debate, Brazil advocated political solutions to conflicts, humanitarian access, food assistance, humanitarian corridors, and measures to reduce civilian harm and conflict-driven food insecurity. It identified indiscriminate explosive attacks, attacks on civilian infrastructure, sexual violence, and risks to women, children, refugees, displaced people, and persons with disabilities.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.4","2B.7","3B.7","6B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly stated by Brazil's foreign minister during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statement represented Brazil's foreign policy under Lula's administration, delivered by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira.","limitations":["The statement records diplomatic positions and advocacy, not a specific peace agreement, military order, or measurable domestic implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1555ec31f18166d5","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"At the 2023 NPT Preparatory Committee, Brazil defended nuclear disarmament, opposed treating the IAEA Additional Protocol as a mandatory new verification standard, supported diplomatic resolution of the DPRK and Iran nuclear issues, and stated that Brazil's naval nuclear propulsion program was subject to discussions with the IAEA and ABACC for special verification procedures. Brazil reported that preliminary design information had been provided and emphasized transparency.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.3","1B.4","1B.8","1B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Brazil's delegation delivered the statement during the July-August 2023 preparatory session.","ruler_attribution":"The statement represented the Lula administration's official diplomatic position.","limitations":["The statement is an official position and progress report; it does not independently verify the adequacy or completion of the safeguards arrangement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1555ec31f18166d5","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Brazil assumed the chairmanship of the Nuclear Suppliers Group in July 2023 and described the role as reflecting its commitment to preventing nuclear proliferation through effective export controls while preserving legitimate nuclear trade and cooperation.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.6","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly reported for July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The action was undertaken by Brazil's government during Lula's administration.","limitations":["The source does not provide specific enforcement actions, detected violations, or measurable effects of the chairmanship."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5a88fb792332c58e","start_unit":19,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"A CNJ study published in May 2023 found severe prison-system risks: tuberculosis detection was up to 30 times higher than in the free population, death risk from cachexia was 1,350% higher, average post-release survival was 548 days, and 28% of post-release deaths occurred in violent events. The study identified underreporting, weak death records, inadequate health services, and limited accountability or reparation, and issued 36 recommendations.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The institutional finding was published during 2023 and concerns the Brazilian prison system.","ruler_attribution":"The CNJ finding concerns state custodial institutions during Lula's 2023 period but does not attribute the failures personally to Lula.","limitations":["The source does not identify which level of government caused each failure or document Lula's response during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5a88fb792332c58e","start_unit":20,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"The CNJ study reported that prison mortality data were poorly communicated and recorded, racial classifications did not align across police, judicial, prison, and IBGE records, and the state lacked reliable information about deaths and human-rights violations, including those linked to state violence or deficient health promotion.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","6B.5","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings were reported in May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Brazilian state institutions; the supplied source does not establish that Lula personally directed the deficiencies.","limitations":["No 2023 corrective action by the executive is documented in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-4d039fd466b41c43","start_unit":11,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"Brazil's Foreign Ministry reported that in 2023 Brazil restored diplomatic relations with Venezuela, reopened its embassy in Caracas and Venezuela's embassy in Brasília, received President Nicolás Maduro in Brasília on 29 May, and hosted him at the South American presidents' meeting on 30 May. It also reported 2023 bilateral trade of US$1.57 billion, including US$1.15 billion in Brazilian exports and US$413 million in imports.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","5B.4","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The diplomatic and trade events are explicitly dated to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The restoration and high-level engagements occurred under Lula's presidency.","limitations":["The source documents restored relations and trade figures but does not assess democratic conditions in Venezuela or the longer-term consequences of the policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0324e309c6214737","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A World Bank policy assessment identified Brazil's inherited fiscal and structural challenges: an unsustainable fiscal path, high tax-system distortions and compliance costs, subnational fiscal crises, unsustainable pension obligations, and state underperformance in health, education, public security, and infrastructure due partly to weak planning, monitoring, evaluation, and rigid budgets.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","6B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in 2018, this is baseline/context evidence predating Lula's 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment concerns Brazil's structural conditions and is not attributed to Lula.","limitations":["It does not show which problems persisted in 2023 or what Lula did in response."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0324e309c6214737","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The World Bank assessment reported that Brazil invested about 2% of GDP in infrastructure, below comparable countries and insufficient to cover depreciation; it also described poor education outcomes despite relatively high spending, high crime and violence despite large security expenditures, and stalled progress in reducing deforestation.","question_ids":["3B.6","5B.6","5B.10","6B.2","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in 2018, this is inherited baseline/context rather than a 2023 measurement.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment does not attribute these conditions to Lula's 2023 administration.","limitations":["The supplied page provides no 2023 update or evidence of Lula-era change."]},{"source_id":"SRC-106e3b7c45d19a3b","start_unit":8,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"The World Bank's poverty and inequality resource explains that poverty is multidimensional, affecting nutrition, education, electricity, sanitation, healthcare, and vulnerability to conflict and climate change; it provides national and international poverty indicators, Gini and income-share measures, and warns that survey coverage, timeliness, comparability, nonresponse, and underrepresentation of poor or homeless households can create uncertainty and bias.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.5","6B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The page includes 2023 data-availability discussion but provides no Brazil-specific 2023 result in the supplied text.","ruler_attribution":"The source is methodological and not attributable to Lula.","limitations":["No concrete Lula-era policy, event, or Brazil-specific quantitative outcome is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-21de7a073c6ec929","start_unit":12,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Lula's government revived Minha Casa, Minha Vida through Provisional Measure 1.162, later converted into Law 14.620. The redesigned program emphasized better-located housing near commerce, public facilities, and public transport; expanded eligible interventions to new construction, rehabilitation, new and used-unit financing, and housing improvements; exempted Bolsa Família and BPC recipients in subsidized Faixa 1 housing from installments; and prioritized women-headed households, disabled and elderly people, children, vulnerable families, disaster-affected households, people experiencing homelessness, domestic-violence survivors, residents of risk areas, and traditional and quilombola peoples.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.7","6B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The program revival and governing law occurred in 2023; the page was later updated and contains some later thresholds, which are not used here.","ruler_attribution":"The program was revived and legislated under Lula's administration.","limitations":["The supplied text describes design and priorities, not completed construction or 2023 housing outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-21de7a073c6ec929","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"For 2023, the subsidized Minha Casa, Minha Vida FAR line set a target of contracting 130,000 new housing units, distributed among states according to housing deficit. The program also established proposal-based participation by local governments or construction companies and provided separate lines for nonprofit entities, rural households, small municipalities, and financed housing.","question_ids":["5B.6","6B.2","6B.3","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The 130,000-unit target and associated 2023 regulations are explicitly tied to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The target and implementation structure were established by Lula's government.","limitations":["A target is not evidence of completed units, spending execution, or equitable delivery."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-366c5ffb6dcdfd63","SRC-7ce89e7e26c821d6"],"batch_limitations":["Several sources are official institutional pages or policy statements and therefore establish formal positions, designs, or findings but not independent causal attribution to Lula personally.","The supplied material contains limited 2023 outcome data; implementation and end-period claims should remain qualified."]}
